task:
BUILD PURGE PR P2a: purge-state fences on every governed production mutator, plus the ledger-aware pgBackRest wrapper and its governed install action. Base on current origin/main; it must be 2bd8e7dc18071f85f87a937be715588669e385a0 (PR #817, migration 016, merged) -- record the SHA you used; if main has moved, use the new head and say so. New branch (no target_branch). Code only: no production access, no deployment, no production credentials, no workflow dispatch.

AUTHORITY: docs/development/v3-governed-derived-purge-design.md, sections 4.2 and 4.3 step 3, and the gate 3b row of section 7 (option (b), read-only writer fence, is selected). Read CLAUDE.md first, then those sections in full, then sql/v3/migrations/016_v3_governed_derived_purge.sql to learn the exact ledger relations, event kinds and payload fields. Purge P2 is split into four PRs: P2a (this one: fences + backup wrapper), P2b (the purge action script with all modes, loop, lease, trap, rewrite monitor), P2c (the protected workflow v3-production-derived-purge.yml and read-only ops choices), P2d (the 1% rehearsal). Do NOT build P2b-P2d here.

BUILD:
1. One shared read-only purge-state check in scripts/operator/lib/ (a shell helper and/or a Python module, whichever the callers need; both may share one fixed SQL text). Fixed SQL only, no identifiers from input. It reports, for the operating database, every unresolved purge state by kind, exactly as design 4.2 defines them: an open BATCH_STARTED or REWRITE_STARTED (no closing BATCH_COMMITTED/BATCH_ROLLED_BACK or REWRITE_VERIFIED/REWRITE_ROLLED_BACK/FAILED_STOP); SERVICES_QUIESCED without SERVICES_RESTORED; WRITER_FENCE_ENABLED without a VERIFIED WRITER_FENCE_RESTORED (match 016's own rule: the restore counts only when its payload has verified=true); AUTOVACUUM_DISABLED without AUTOVACUUM_RESTORED; and any FAILED_STOP with integrity_failed=true. Reuse 016's own definitions where it exposes a function or view; do not re-derive them differently. It also probes the host lease /run/lock/edfinder-v3-derived-purge.lock with a non-blocking flock and reports held/free. Any unresolved state or a held lease means REFUSE. A query failure means REFUSE.
2. Absent ledger relation (v3_meta.derived_generation_purge_event does not exist) is a REFUSAL for every caller except one bootstrap case owned by the schema-migration apply alone: the apply proceeds when the live migration ledger is exactly the prefix the authenticated plan was built against AND the plan's complete pending suffix ends in 016_v3_governed_derived_purge.sql. Once 016 is recorded as applied, or when the pending suffix does not end in 016, an absent relation refuses. Key this to the plan's recorded prefix, not to a fixed migration name list.
3. Call the check FIRST (before any mutation, before any lock or container change) in every governed production mutator: the application deployer (scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py mutating operations and scripts/operator/actions/v3-production-promote.sh), the derived-product publisher (scripts/operator/actions/v3-publish-derived-products.sh), the schema-migration apply (scripts/operator/actions/v3-production-migrate.sh / scripts/operator/v3_production_migrate.py, with the bootstrap rule), the spatial publisher (scripts/operator/actions/v3-spatial-pyramid.sh), and every ops-workflow action that starts or launches a worker or writes production state (inspect each script under scripts/operator/actions/ called by .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml -- at least ratings-v4-generation.sh, v3-system-search-f1.sh, v3-system-archetype.sh, v3-system-search-validate-constraints.sh, v3-archetype-calibration-complete.sh; list which you classed as mutators and which as read-only, with a reason for each). Read-only status/inventory/probe actions do not call it. Each mutator also refuses while the purge host lease is held. The refusal output is the caller's existing JSON receipt shape with a clear failure code naming the unresolved kind(s).
4. Ledger-aware deploy/v3-production/backup/pgbackrest-operation.sh: before starting any backup or verify, run fixed read-only SQL through the same docker exec path the wrapper already uses, with exactly `psql -X --no-psqlrc --no-password --username edfinder_v3 --dbname edfinder_v3_phase4c_full_20260827_r5` (confirm those pinned names against scripts/operator/actions/v3-system-search-validate-constraints.sh). It takes the existing SKIP path, and logs which open record it skipped for, while an unresolved BATCH_STARTED or REWRITE_STARTED names a backend whose recorded PID AND backend_start are both still present in pg_stat_activity. An open record with a dead backend does NOT skip. If the query fails, or the ledger relation is absent, the wrapper exits non-zero before starting anything (same as its existing pgbackrest info check). Keep the wrapper standalone: it runs from the installed /opt/ed-finder-v3-runtime/ copy, not a repo checkout, so the SQL lives inside it. Update deploy/v3-production/backup/README.md.
5. New allowlisted operator action scripts/operator/actions/v3-backup-wrapper-install.sh, added as a choice on .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml using the same trusted-main streaming pattern as v3-disk-inventory. It pins host/FQDN, the destination /opt/ed-finder-v3-runtime/pgbackrest-operation.sh and the source SHA; refuses while /run/lock/edfinder-v3-pgbackrest-schedule.lock is held or any pgbackrest backup/verify process runs in the PostgreSQL container; REFUSES unless migration 016 is recorded as applied and the ledger relation exists (otherwise the new wrapper would fail every scheduled backup); writes the committed file to a temp path with mode 0700, verifies its SHA-256 against the committed source, renames it into place atomically, re-reads and re-verifies the installed hash, and emits a JSON receipt with both hashes and explicit write booleans. It changes no timer or unit.
6. Tests: tests/test_v3_derived_generation_purge_operator.py (new; P2b will extend it) with a contract test per mutator that it refuses on each unresolved kind and on a held lease, and that the migration apply's bootstrap case passes only in the exact case above and refuses in both counter-cases; bash -n on every changed script; tests for the wrapper skip logic (skips with a live recorded backend and an open record; runs once the backend is gone; runs with no open record; fails rather than skips when the relation is absent or the query fails; uses the pinned --username/--dbname); install-action contract tests (pins, refusals, atomic rename, hash verification, receipt schema, no secrets, strict SSH unchanged). Where a disposable PostgreSQL 18 test is the right proof (the shared SQL against a real 016 ledger), add it to tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py or a new PG18 test file following that file's fixtures; PG18 tests may skip on the runner -- report them as written-not-run. Update any existing contract tests whose asserted command text legitimately changes; do not weaken them.
7. Docs: a short runbook section in docs/operations/ (find the current V3 purge or schema-migration runbook; if none fits, add docs/operations/v3-governed-derived-purge.md) covering the fences and the wrapper install order: apply 016, dispatch v3-backup-wrapper-install, commit its receipt, then the purge plan. CHANGES.md entry.

RULES: exact CPython 3.14; fail-closed; parameterized SQL; no secrets; no ssh-keyscan; do not weaken host verification or broaden allowlists beyond the one new action; no production operation. Run: ruff check .; python -m pytest -q on every test file you touched plus tests/test_v3_production_migration_operation.py, tests/test_v3_lineage_migrations.py and the deploy/release-gate tests; python scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py --operation authority-gate (expect no failures).

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING, complete in this order and stop cleanly: (1) shared check + migration-apply bootstrap rule + deployer/promote/publisher refusals with tests; (2) remaining mutators; (3) ledger-aware wrapper + tests; (4) install action + workflow choice + tests; (5) docs. End with: base SHA; files changed; the mutator/read-only classification table; tests run with counts; PG18 tests written but not run; every design-versus-current-code conflict; and anything left.
